words.definition: Assistance and advice provided by a company to people who buy or use its products or services.
Money lent or made available under a credit arrangement.
An estimate of income and expenditure for a set period of time.
A record or statement of financial expenditure or receipts relating to a particular period or purpose.
Something borrowed, especially a sum of money expected to be paid back with interest.
A right to keep possession of another person's property until a debt owed by that person is discharged.
A formal decision-making process used when considering the economic feasibility of implementing controls and safeguards.
Non-repayable funds or products disbursed by one party to another.
A general agreement.
The personnel of a business or organisation, especially when regarded as a significant asset.
The action or process of investing money for profit or material result.
Economic activity concerned with processing raw materials and making goods in factories.
A group elected to represent stockholders, establish corporate management policies and make decisions on major company issues.
Wealth in the form of money or other assets owned by a person or organisation, or available for a particular purpose.
The value of the shares issued by a company.
Wealth in the form of money or other assets owned by a person or organisation.
An amount of money added to wages, especially as a reward for good performance.
The rate or value of the shares issued by a company.
A person who starts an enterprise.
The action or process of keeping financial accounts.
The practice of making one's living by engaging in commerce.
A sum deposited with a broker to cover the risk of loss on a transaction or account.
The detailed coordination of a complex operation involving many people, facilities or supplies.
A person who takes a franchise and operates under a contract or licensing agreement with the franchiser.
The parent company that grants the franchise and provides goods and services.
A business system in which an operator obtains the right to use an established business name, brand or model.
A business owned by one person.
A business owned by two or more individuals.
A person who owns shares in a corporation.
A unit of ownership in a corporation.
A sum of money paid to shareholders; the part of a corporation's profit after taxes distributed to shareholders.
A process in which two businesses combine into one business or legal entity.
A process whereby one company combines with or takes over the ownership of another.
A business project or arrangement in which two or more parties combine skills or resources for a shared project.
An agreement between businesses to commit resources to achieve common objectives.
A condition in which owners' losses are limited to the amount they invested; personal assets are not used to cover business debts.
A condition in which responsibility for business debts can extend beyond the amount invested.
The net value of property or assets after subtracting mortgage or other liabilities.
A borrower's ability to carry debt and pay it when due.
A borrower's assets that can be used to repay a debt.
The relocation or transfer of some of a company's operations or functions to another company.
The practice of outsourcing or moving operations overseas.
A business organisation with operations in more than one country.
A business in which economic transactions are conducted within the geographical boundaries of one country.
A business model that allows companies and individuals to buy and sell goods and services over the internet.
Money available to fund day-to-day operations and support future expansion.
An activity or benefit supplied to customers, usually in return for payment, rather than a physical product.
A corporation that does not offer its shares of stock to the public for purchase.
A corporation that offers its shares of stock for public sale.
A formal written summary of a business and/or financial security provided to potential investors.
